tagline: Down the switchbacks to the rock that tells a story.
intro: SR-211 leaves US 191 fourteen miles north of Monticello, near Church Rock, and heads west across the high sage plain and through Photograph Gap. Then it drops, steeply and through tight turns, into the canyon. Below the switchbacks the road follows Indian Creek between Wingate sandstone walls and open ranch land toward the Needles District of Canyonlands.
Much of the open land on either side is The Nature Conservancy's Dugout Ranch, kept free of development, and the canyon walls are a popular climbing ground.

moments.title: Home of Truth
moments.text: Empty buildings on fenced land mark the colony the spiritualist Marie Ogden founded here in 1933, which came apart after she wrote of efforts to raise a woman from the dead.

moments.title: Newspaper Rock
moments.text: Right off the shoulder, a cliff face carries more than 650 designs, most carved from about the start of the current era to 1300, many apparently showing an extra toe or finger.

moments.title: Bridger Jack Butte
moments.text: A sandstone butte named for a Paiute medicine man stands more than 700 feet above Lavender Canyon, in sight of the road on the way to the Needles.

practical: Because of the steep, sharply curved descent into the canyon, vehicles wider than 10 feet or longer than 80 feet must have a pilot car escort on SR-211.
